long_post.full_text:
Spent the week rebuilding a small notes app from scratch. The first version kept everything in one giant file, and every save rewrote the whole thing. That was fine at fifty notes and painful at five thousand.

The fix was boring: one file per note, an index on the side, and a lock around writes. Search went from four seconds to forty milliseconds.

The part nobody warns you about is migration. Old notes had three date formats and a few had none. I wrote a tiny checker that lists the odd ones instead of guessing.

Full write-up with the checker script: https://example.com/notes-checker FULL-TEXT-END

Second, the microphone arm is clamped to the wall, not the desk, so typing no longer thumps into every take. Third, cables run through one tray.

Total cost was under a hundred dollars and an afternoon. MEDIA-TEXT-END

quoted_post.quote_full_text:
A short guide to naming things in a codebase you will read again in a year. Name a function for what it promises, not how it works today. Name a flag for the state it describes, never for the bug that made you add it. Keep one word per idea across the whole project, and write the word down in the readme so new people use it too.

If a name needs a comment, the name is not done yet. QUOTE-TEXT-END
